thread:
Maya R.: Heads-up — planning a rolling control-plane switchover + NIC thermal mitigation in us-central1 tonight 00:30-02:30 UTC. We'll operate in 6-GPU cohorts, cordon+drain, reboot NICs, validate egress and model-serving tail latency. Expected capacity reduction ~18% while cohorts are offline. Ticket: INFRA-8271. CC @Ashwin K., @Laura C.

InfraBot: Scheduled maintenance ticket INFRA-8271 created. Window: 2026-03-29 00:30–02:30 UTC. Automated runbook attached.

Ashwin K.: Ack — I'm on call that window. I'll own Prometheus/Alertmanager watches and BGP checks. Will prepare canary route swap.

Laura C.: Quick Q — any cross-region backfill or live Dedicated customers hitting us-central1 that need pre-notice?

Maya R.: Good call. We have two mid-size Dedicated tenants with steady traffic (avg 120 qps each) plus ongoing eu->us-sync for embeddings. Plan: pre-warm eu-west1 burst pool and reduce us-central1 batch autoscaler target by 12% for the window.

Ben S.: Recommend adding ephemeral burst pool in eu-west1 and enabling spillover routing. Also propose lowering default batch size for the window to keep tail latency predictable.

Laura C.: Sounds good. How long do we expect each cohort to be offline?

Maya R.: ~8–12 minutes per node including drain + reboot + checks. Total for cohort ~50–70 minutes including rollout and verification.

Ashwin K.: Playbook (condensed):
```
# mark cohort
python infra/tools/mark_cohort.py --pool us-central1-pool-A --cohort 3
# scale down noncritical jobs
kubectl scale deployment batch-workers -n inference --replicas=30
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon node-abc123
kubectl drain node-abc123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# remote NIC reboot
ssh mgmt@node-abc123 'sudo /usr/local/bin/nic-reboot && sudo journalctl -u nic -n 200'
# post-checks
curl -sS http://edge-probe/latency -w 'time_total=%{time_total}\n'
```

Ashwin K.: I'll run the canary on the first cohort and hold for 15m. If Prometheus p95 model latency jumps >150ms or error rate >0.7%, we abort and fallback to previous control plane.

Maya R.: Add ticket note: unit-cost estimate — rolling will consume ~420 GPU-minutes extra due to rebalancing and temporary replication overhead; cost delta ~+$380 for window. Worth it given thermal failure risk.

Ben S.: Acknowledge cost. We can offset by deferring a small noncritical batch sweep scheduled at 01:00 UTC. I'll push that to later.

Laura C.: I'll send customer comms draft to #customer-success after ops sign-off. Minimal impact wording: "possible intermittent latency increases in us-central1 during maintenance window".

Oncall Pager: Pager reminders scheduled. I'll post an update at T-30 and T+10.

Maya R.: Final checks: please verify the following before greenlight:
- Canaries passing (p95 < 120ms)
- BGP peer flaps = 0 during swap
- No queued Dedicated job failures in last 30m

Ashwin K.: Understood. I'll post canary results here.

InfraBot: Maintenance INFRA-8271 reminders: T-60, T-30, T-10 posted. Auto rollback hook enabled.

Ben S.: thumbs up :thumbsup: 

Laura C.: acked :white_check_mark: 

Maya R.: Thanks — will start cohort tagging at 00:10 UTC and start first cordon at 00:30. Ping here for any anomalies.

Ashwin K.: Canary results after cohort 1: p95=98ms, error rate=0.12%, BGP stable. Moving to cohort 2.

Maya R.: Noted. Continuing rollout.

Ashwin K.: Cohort 2 smoke: p95 spike to 160ms for ~40s during pod rescheduling, recovered. No customer-facing errors. Still within abort thresholds. Proceeding.

Maya R.: Proceed with caution for remaining cohorts. Keep me posted.

Oncall Pager: All cohorts completed. Post-checks green. Closing INFRA-8271.

Laura C.: Sending customer comms now. Good job team.
